subject: science
passage: A bolt of lightning heats the air around it to an astonishing ______ roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius, several times hotter than the surface of the sun. The heated air expands so violently that it sends out a shock wave, which we hear as thunder.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A bolt of lightning heats the air around it to an astonishing temperature" is a complete sentence. "Roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius" is not a clause but a phrase that states exactly what that temperature is. A colon placed after a complete sentence introduces such an explanation or detail.
explanation.A: Correct. A colon after the complete sentence introduces the phrase that specifies the temperature.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on each side; "roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius" is only a phrase.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "And" would join "temperature" and "roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius" as if they were two separate things, which makes no sense; the second phrase explains the first.
explanation.D: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the phrase "roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius" runs into the sentence with nothing to connect it.
